title: MCP Doesn't Suck. Your Agent Does. — Jan Čurn, Apify
talk_summary: Speaker argues MCP's context bloat is a harness problem, not a protocol problem, and recommends progressive tool discovery, code mode, and a CLI wrapper (MCPC) that hides MCP behind bash. He also presents connector-level evals comparing raw MCP, CLI, and MCPC on time and token cost.

takeaways.what_they_do: Instead of registering all tool schemas up front, expose a search/grep tool that finds relevant tools and loads only those into context.
takeaways.evidence_quote: put those tools into the context progressively only when you need them

takeaways.what_they_do: Wrap MCP/remote tools as CLI commands with --json output and agent-readable help; agents compose them in bash/jq instead of loading tool schemas.
takeaways.evidence_quote: full complexity of MCP is hidden behind single tool call bash
takeaways.numbers: Connector evals: MCPC and CLI similar; raw MCP faster but more tokens (no exact figures)

takeaways.what_they_do: Benchmark connector interfaces (raw MCP, CLI, wrapper) on the same tasks, measuring wall time and token cost rather than only model quality.
takeaways.numbers: Charts compare time vs token cost; no exact values in transcript

takeaways.what_they_do: Use MCP for standardized remote access/auth/sessions, but use CLI for local agent interface because agents know shell and CLI is code-mode by default.
takeaways.evidence_quote: MCP for standard remote access and CLI for local agent access

takeaways.technique: Async task handles for long tools
takeaways.what_they_do: Start long-running tool work as an async server task, detach, then poll progress and collect results later instead of blocking the agent run.
takeaways.evidence_quote: run this task asynchronously that means like it starts on the server

takeaways.technique: Keep secrets and large data out of context
takeaways.what_they_do: Treat model context as a bad place for sensitive values or large payloads; subagents only push the problem further, so pass references and inject credentials in the tool runtime.
takeaways.evidence_quote: context is is is a really bad place to uh pass sensitive value
